title: Enforcement Decree of the Act on the Prevention of Insolvency and Structural Improvement of Fisheries Cooperatives
title_original: 수산업협동조합의 부실예방 및 구조개선에 관한 법률 시행령
full_text:
Article 1 (Purpose) The purpose of this Decree is to prescribe matters delegated by the Act on the Prevention of Insolvency and Structural Improvement of Fisheries Cooperatives and matters necessary for its enforcement. <Amended on August 19, 2020>

Article 2 (Persons Excluded from the Scope of Deposits, etc.) “Amounts received from the Government, local governments, and other persons prescribed by Presidential Decree” in the proviso to the portion of Article 2, subparagraph 6 of the Act on the Prevention of Insolvency and Structural Improvement of Fisheries Cooperatives (hereinafter referred to as the “Act”) other than its items means amounts received from any of the following persons: <Amended on March 11, 2016; May 10, 2016; August 19, 2020>
1. The Government and local governments;
2. The Bank of Korea established under the Bank of Korea Act, the Financial Supervisory Service established under the Act on the Establishment, etc. of Financial Services Commission, and the Korea Deposit Insurance Corporation established under the Depositor Protection Act;
3. Insured financial companies under Article 2, subparagraph 1 of the Depositor Protection Act;
4. Cooperatives.

Article 2-2 (Measures Concerning Changes to Prompt Corrective Measures) “Measures prescribed by Presidential Decree, such as a management diagnosis” in the latter part of the portion of Article 4-3 of the Act other than its subparagraphs means any of the following measures:
1. A management diagnosis;
2. Suspension or recovery of financial assistance to the cooperative concerned;
3. Other measures for changing the prompt corrective measures under Article 4-2 of the Act (hereinafter referred to as “prompt corrective measures”), or measures following such changes, that the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries considers necessary.

Article 3 (Contents of Agreements to Implement Management Normalization)
① “Financial soundness standards prescribed by Presidential Decree” in Article 9 (2) 1 of the Act means the ratio of net capital to total assets prescribed for cooperatives by the Financial Services Commission under Article 83-3 (1) 1 of the Credit Unions Act. In such cases, loan loss allowances and non-performing claims relevant to calculating the ratio of net capital to total assets shall include those arising from businesses other than credit business.
② “Profitability standards prescribed by Presidential Decree” in Article 9 (2) 2 of the Act means the following standards:
1. Return on assets or capital;
2. The ratio of expenses to revenue;
3. Productivity per officer or employee.
③ “Matters prescribed by Presidential Decree” in Article 9 (2) 4 of the Act means matters concerning an increase in equity capital.
④ Specific standards for the ratio of net capital to total assets under paragraph (1), return on assets or capital and other matters under paragraph (2), an increase in equity capital under paragraph (3), and other such matters shall be determined by the Fund Management Committee under Article 21 of the Act (hereinafter referred to as the “Fund Management Committee”).
⑤ Deleted. <December 23, 2014>

Article 4 (Non-Disclosure of Agreements) “Matters prescribed by Presidential Decree” in the proviso to Article 9 (3) of the Act means any of the following matters:
1. Matters concerning the sale of assets held, such as real estate and claims;
2. Matters concerning methods for implementing a management normalization plan.

Article 5 (Explanations Concerning Administrative Dispositions) When giving an insolvent cooperative an opportunity to provide explanations under the proviso to Article 10 (2) of the Act, the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall dispatch to the cooperative, no later than 10 days before the date for providing explanations, a notice stating the contents of the disposition, the deadline and method for providing explanations, how the matter will be handled if no explanation is provided, and other matters necessary for providing explanations. <Amended on March 23, 2013>

Article 6 (Determination of Estimated Payment Rates and Estimated Amounts, etc.)
① When purchasing claims on deposits, etc. under Article 13 (1) of the Act, the management agency under Article 22 of the Act (hereinafter referred to as the “management agency”) shall determine an estimated payment rate, taking into account the cooperative's financial condition and estimating the amount that could be repaid on claims on deposits, etc. relating to that cooperative if bankruptcy proceedings are conducted.
② The estimated value of claims on deposits, etc. that the management agency is required to pay to depositors, etc. under Article 13 (2) of the Act shall be calculated by multiplying the value of the claims on deposits, etc. purchased from depositors, etc., calculated as of the date of public notice of payment of insurance proceeds (excluding claims on deposits, etc. corresponding to the guarantee obligations of depositors, etc. who bear such obligations and the amount of claims on deposits, etc. that are the subject of security rights), by the estimated payment rate under paragraph (1).
③ To pay depositors, etc. the estimated value of claims on deposits, etc. under Article 13 (2) of the Act, the management agency shall determine the estimated payment rate under paragraph (1), the period and method of purchasing the claims, and other such matters, and obtain a resolution of the Fund Management Committee.
④ After obtaining a resolution under paragraph (3), the management agency shall publish a public notice at least once in each of at least two daily newspapers, including one daily newspaper registered under Article 9 (1) of the Act on the Promotion of Newspapers, etc. with the area in which the cooperative's principal office is located as its main circulation area, or post it on the management agency's website or other such media. <Amended on November 24, 2020>

Article 7 (Largest Creditor) “Largest creditor prescribed by Presidential Decree” in Article 15 (1) of the Act means the person who, following an investigation of the cooperative's financial position as of any of the following dates, holds the largest amount of claims against the cooperative {including claims resulting from payment of insurance proceeds, purchase of claims on deposits, etc., financial assistance, or other such actions by the Mutual Finance Depositor Protection Fund established and operated under Article 20 of the Act (hereinafter referred to as the “Fund”) after the date of business suspension, the decision to transfer contracts, the resolution to dissolve, or revocation of authorization for establishment}:
1. A cooperative dissolved due to bankruptcy: the date of business suspension;
2. A cooperative dissolved due to a transfer of contracts: the date of the decision to transfer contracts;
3. A cooperative dissolved for another reason: the date of the resolution to dissolve or revocation of authorization for establishment.

Article 8 (Requests to Obtain Liability Insurance)
① “A cooperative meeting the criteria prescribed by Presidential Decree” in Article 17 (1) of the Act means a cooperative that, as a result of the assessment of its management condition by the president of the National Federation of Fisheries Cooperatives (Federation) under Article 142 (2) of the Fisheries Cooperatives Act, fails to meet the standards determined by the Fund Management Committee.
② When requesting a cooperative to obtain liability insurance under Article 17 (1) of the Act, the management agency shall make the request in writing, specifying the maximum insurance proceeds payable and other matters determined by the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries. <Amended on March 23, 2013>
③ A cooperative requested by the management agency to obtain liability insurance under Article 17 (1) of the Act shall obtain such insurance within six months from the date of the request. However, where unavoidable circumstances recognized by the Fund Management Committee exist, such as where obtaining liability insurance is considered likely to make normal management difficult, the cooperative shall obtain the insurance within a period determined by the management agency, not exceeding two years.

Article 9 (Methods and Procedures of Investigation)
① If necessary to conduct an investigation under Article 18 (7) of the Act, the management agency may have its employees examine books, documents, and other materials concerning the business and property condition of the legal entity in liquidation or bankruptcy estate of an insolvent cooperative or a cooperative at risk of insolvency.
② When conducting an investigation under paragraph (1), the management agency shall notify the person subject to investigation in advance of the reasons for and scope of the investigation and other necessary matters. This shall not apply where advance notice would create a risk of destruction of evidence or other circumstances that would prevent the purpose of the investigation from being achieved.
③ When conducting an investigation under paragraph (1), the management agency shall give the person subject to investigation a sufficient opportunity to state an opinion.
④ Upon completing an investigation, the management agency shall notify the party concerned of the results in writing.

Article 10 (Types of Public Institutions) “Public institutions prescribed by Presidential Decree” in Article 19 of the Act means the following institutions:
1. Public institutions under the Act on the Management of Public Institutions;
2. Legal entities established under special Acts;
3. Clearing houses designated under the Bills of Exchange and Promissory Notes Act or the Check Act.

Article 11 (Operation of the Fund Management Committee)
① The chairperson of the Fund Management Committee shall convene and preside over its meetings.
② If the chairperson is unable to perform duties for unavoidable reasons, the vice-chairperson and then a member determined by the Fund Management Committee shall perform those duties, in that order.
③ A meeting of the Fund Management Committee shall open with a majority of its incumbent members present, and resolutions shall be adopted with the approval of a majority of the members present.
④ A member of the Fund Management Committee shall be excluded from its deliberation and resolution on an agenda item in any of the following cases: <Newly inserted on August 19, 2020>
1. The member or the member's spouse or former spouse is a party to the agenda item;
2. The member is or was a relative of a party to the agenda item;
3. The member has provided testimony, a statement, research, services, an expert appraisal, or advice on the agenda item;
4. The member belongs, or has belonged within the past three years, to a cooperative, enterprise, organization, or other such body related to the agenda item.
⑤ If a member has a ground for exclusion under any subparagraph of paragraph (4), or there are other circumstances making it difficult to expect impartial deliberation and resolution, a party to the agenda item may apply to the Fund Management Committee to challenge that member, and the Committee shall decide by resolution whether to uphold the challenge. The member challenged shall not participate in that resolution. <Newly inserted on August 19, 2020>
⑥ A member with a ground for exclusion under any subparagraph of paragraph (4) shall voluntarily recuse himself or herself from deliberation and resolution on the agenda item. <Newly inserted on August 19, 2020>
⑦ A person who commissioned or designated a member under any subparagraph of Article 21 (2) of the Act may dismiss that member or withdraw the designation if the member fails to recuse himself or herself despite having a ground for exclusion under any subparagraph of paragraph (4). <Newly inserted on August 19, 2020>
⑧ Matters necessary for operation of the Fund Management Committee, other than those provided in paragraphs (1) through (7), shall be determined by the Committee. <Amended on August 19, 2020>

Article 12 (Issuance of Mutual Finance Depositor Protection Fund Bonds, etc.) Articles 42 and 43, Article 44 (1), Article 44 (2) 1 through 6, 8 and 9, Articles 45 through 51, Articles 54 through 56, and Articles 58 and 59 of the Enforcement Decree of the Fisheries Cooperatives Act shall apply mutatis mutandis to the issuance, offering for subscription, and other related matters concerning Mutual Finance Depositor Protection Fund bonds (hereinafter referred to as “Fund bonds”) issued by the management agency at the expense of the Fund under Article 27 (2) of the Act. In such cases, “Federation” shall be construed as “management agency”; “bonds” as “Fund bonds”; “president, chief executive officer in charge of a business sector, or president of Suhyup Bank” as “head of the management agency”; and “board of directors” as “Fund Management Committee.” <Amended on October 25, 2016>

Article 13 (Calculation and Payment of Insurance Premiums)
① Under Article 29 (1) of the Act, a cooperative shall pay to the Fund the insurance premiums calculated using the following formulas within one month after the end of each quarter. However, premiums for mutual insurance business shall be paid within three months after the end of each business year. <Amended on March 23, 2013>
1. Insurance premium for credit business = average balance of deposits and installment savings at the end of each quarter × 1/4 × the rate determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries within 5/1,000;
2. Insurance premium for mutual insurance business = (balance of policy reserves at the end of each business year + total mutual insurance premiums received at the end of each business year) × 1/2 × the rate determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries within 5/1,000.
② Deposits, etc. received from the persons specified in the subparagraphs of Article 2 shall be excluded when calculating the premiums for credit business and mutual insurance business under paragraph (1).
③ If a cooperative fails to pay the premium under paragraph (1) by the payment deadline, it shall pay it to the Fund with an added late fee equal to the number of days from the day following the payment deadline to the date of payment multiplied by the interest rate determined by the Fund Management Committee based on the interest rate for mutual finance loans made by the Federation to cooperatives. <Amended on December 23, 2014>

Article 13-2 (Reduction and Exemption of Insurance Premiums)
① Under Article 29-2 (4) of the Act, if the Fund's accumulated amount as of the last day of the preceding fiscal year is at least the lower limit of the target accumulated amount established or re-established under Article 29-2 (1) through (3) of the Act (hereinafter in this Article referred to as the “target amount”), the management agency shall reduce the premiums for the fiscal year concerned following a resolution of the Fund Management Committee.
② Under Article 29-2 (4) of the Act, if the Fund's accumulated amount as of the last day of the preceding fiscal year exceeds the upper limit of the target amount, the management agency may exempt cooperatives from premiums for the fiscal year concerned following a resolution of the Fund Management Committee.
③ Details of the procedures and methods for reducing or exempting premiums under paragraphs (1) and (2) shall be determined by the management agency following a resolution of the Fund Management Committee.

Article 14 (Calculation of Insurance Proceeds) When calculating insurance proceeds payable by the management agency at the request of depositors, etc. under Articles 30 (1) and 31 (1) of the Act, the aggregate amount of claims on deposits, etc. shall be the sum of the following amounts:
1. The amount of deposits, etc.;
2. The amount in subparagraph 1 multiplied by the interest rate determined by the Fund Management Committee, taking into account the average interest rate on deposits, etc. of all cooperatives.

Article 15 (Advance Payments) Under Article 30 (2) of the Act, the management agency may pay depositors, etc., in advance, an amount determined by the Fund Management Committee within the limit on insurance proceeds under Article 18 (hereinafter referred to as an “advance payment”). However, if the advance payment exceeds the insurance proceeds calculated under Article 31 (1) of the Act, those insurance proceeds shall be the maximum amount payable.

Article 16 (Public Notice of Procedures for Payment of Insurance Proceeds, etc.) Under Article 30 (3) of the Act, the management agency shall give public notice of the commencement date, period, and method of payment of insurance proceeds and advance payments, and other necessary matters, by applying Article 6 (4) mutatis mutandis.

Article 17 (Withholding of Insurance Proceeds)
① “Amounts prescribed by Presidential Decree” in Article 30 (6) of the Act means the following amounts:
1. The amount of claims on deposits, etc. that depositors, etc. have provided to the cooperative concerned as collateral for another person;
2. The amount of guarantee obligations owed by depositors, etc. to the cooperative concerned.
② When withholding insurance proceeds for the amounts under paragraph (1) pursuant to Article 30 (6) of the Act, the management agency shall inform the depositors, etc. who requested payment of the following matters in writing, through an information and communications network, by mobile telephone text message, or by other such means: <Amended on December 23, 2014>
1. The amount of insurance proceeds being withheld;
2. The reason for withholding;
3. The period of withholding;
4. The procedures and methods for depositors, etc. to request payment of the withheld proceeds when the reason for withholding ceases to exist or the withholding period expires.

Article 18 (Limit on Insurance Proceeds) The limit on insurance proceeds under Article 31 (2) of the Act shall be as follows: <Amended on July 29, 2025>
1. For claims on deposits, etc. falling under Article 2, subparagraph 8 (a) of the Act: 100 million Korean won;
2. For claims on deposits, etc. falling under Article 2, subparagraph 8 (b) of the Act: 100 million Korean won separately for each of the following categories of claims:
(a) Claims on deposits, etc. payable under mutual insurance contracts for pension savings accounts under Article 40-2 (1) 1 (c) of the Enforcement Decree of the Income Tax Act (including mutual insurance contracts for pension savings accounts under Article 41 of the Addenda to the Partial Amendment to the Restriction of Special Taxation Act, Act No. 11614);
(b) Mutual insurance benefits payable because grounds for payment under a mutual insurance contract have arisen (excluding contracts under item (a) and benefits payable upon expiration of the mutual insurance period);
(c) Claims on deposits, etc. falling under Article 2, subparagraph 8 (b) of the Act, other than those in items (a) and (b).

Article 19 (Entrustment of Authority) Under Article 35 of the Act, the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall entrust the following authority to the head of the management agency: <Amended on March 23, 2013; August 19, 2020>
1. Designation, management, and cancellation of designation of cooperatives subject to management supervision under Articles 3-3 through 3-5 of the Act;
1-2. Designation of cooperatives at risk of insolvency under Article 4 (2) of the Act;
2. Recommendations or requests for prompt corrective measures under Article 4-2 of the Act for cooperatives at risk of insolvency and their officers.

Article 20 (Processing of Unique Identifying Information)
① The Minister of Oceans and Fisheries (including persons entrusted with the Minister's authority under Article 35 of the Act and Article 19 of this Decree) may process materials containing resident registration numbers, passport numbers, driver's license numbers, or alien registration numbers under Article 19 of the Enforcement Decree of the Personal Information Protection Act, if unavoidable for performing any of the following functions: <Amended on August 19, 2020>
1. Functions concerning designation of insolvent cooperatives or cooperatives at risk of insolvency under Article 4 (2) of the Act;
2. Functions concerning appointment of administrators under Article 4-2 (1) 4, the former part of Article 10 (1), Article 10 (5), and Article 12 (2) of the Act, and requests for registration under Article 12 (5) of the Act;
3. Functions concerning mergers under Article 4-2 (1) 6 of the Act, transfers of business and contracts under subparagraph 7 of the same paragraph, and transfers of contracts under Article 10 (2) of the Act;
4. Deleted. <August 19, 2020>
5. Functions concerning requests for materials or information under Article 19 of the Act;
6. Functions concerning reports and inspections under Article 34 of the Act.
② The Governor of the Financial Supervisory Service established under the Act on the Establishment, etc. of Financial Services Commission may process materials containing resident registration numbers, passport numbers, driver's license numbers, or alien registration numbers under Article 19 of the Enforcement Decree of the Personal Information Protection Act, if unavoidable for performing inspection functions under Article 34 (3) of the Act.
③ Deleted. <August 19, 2020>
④ The management agency may process materials containing resident registration numbers, passport numbers, driver's license numbers, or alien registration numbers under Article 19 of the Enforcement Decree of the Personal Information Protection Act, if unavoidable for performing any of the following functions: <Amended on August 19, 2020>
1. Functions concerning requests for designation of insolvent cooperatives or cooperatives at risk of insolvency under Article 4 (1) of the Act;
2. Functions concerning requests for dismissal or suspension of duties of cooperative officers, and disciplinary action against employees, under Article 9-2 (3) of the Act;
3. Functions concerning presentation of the Fund Management Committee's opinion on appointment of administrators under the former part of Article 10 (1) of the Act;
4. Functions concerning presentation of the Fund Management Committee's opinion on transfers of contracts under the main clause of the portion of Article 10 (2) of the Act other than its subparagraphs;
5. Functions concerning purchase of claims on deposits, etc. under Article 13 of the Act;
6. Functions concerning appointment of liquidators under Article 15 (1) of the Act and recommendation of bankruptcy trustees under paragraph (2) of the same Article;
7. Functions concerning set-off by subrogation under Article 16 of the Act;
8. Functions concerning requests to claim damages under Article 18 (1) of the Act, claims for damages under paragraph (3) of the same Article, and intervention in litigation under the former part of paragraph (4) of the same Article;
9. Functions concerning receipt of insurance premiums under Article 29 (1) of the Act and Article 13 (1) of this Decree;
10. Functions concerning payment of insurance proceeds and other matters under Article 30 of the Act;
11. Functions concerning acquisition of the rights of depositors, etc. under Article 33 of the Act.

Article 21 (Standards for Imposition of Administrative Fines) The standards for imposition of administrative fines under Article 39 (1) through (3) of the Act shall be as set out in the attached Table.

ENFORCEMENT DECREE OF THE ACT ON THE PREVENTION OF INSOLVENCY AND STRUCTURAL IMPROVEMENT OF FISHERIES COOPERATIVES [ATTACHED TABLE] <Newly inserted May 10, 2016>

Criteria for Imposing Administrative Fines (Related to Article 21)

1. General criteria
(a) In any of the following cases, the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries may reduce an administrative fine by up to one half of the amount prescribed in paragraph 2. However, this shall not apply where the administrative fine is in arrears.
1) Where the violator falls under any subparagraph of Article 2-2 (1) of the Enforcement Decree of the Act on the Regulation of Violations of Public Order;
2) Where the violation is considered to have resulted from minor negligence or error;
3) Where the consequences of the violation have been corrected or eliminated;
4) Where a reduction of the administrative fine is otherwise considered necessary in light of the seriousness of the violation, its motives, its consequences, and other circumstances.
(b) Where an increase is considered necessary in light of the seriousness of the violation, its motives, its consequences, and other circumstances, the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries may increase the administrative fine by up to one half of the amount prescribed in paragraph 2.

2. Individual criteria

Unit: 10,000 Korean won (KRW)

| Violation | Legal basis | Administrative fine (units of KRW 10,000) |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| (a) A cooperative fails to make a public announcement under Article 11 (2) of the Act. | Article 39 (1) 1 of the Act | 1,000 |
| (b) A cooperative fails to keep and manage materials under Article 11 (6) of the Act. | Article 39 (1) 2 of the Act | 1,000 |
| (c) A cooperative fails to make materials available for inspection under Article 11 (6) of the Act. | Article 39 (1) 2 of the Act | 500 |
| (d) A cooperative fails to notify the management agency of the occurrence of an insured event under Article 32 (1) of the Act. | Article 39 (1) 3 of the Act | 1,000 |
| (e) A cooperative's chairperson, executive director, administrator, or liquidator violates Article 11 (2) or (6) of the Act. | Article 39 (2) of the Act | 500 |
